newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH C.BANK SELLS PLN 339 MLN BONDS AT OUTRIGHT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH C.BANK SELLS PLN 339 MLN BONDS AT OUTRIGHT.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland sold 161 million zlotys of 17-percent two-year fixed bonds, due July 12, 1997, after Polish banks bid for 225 million of the bonds, the central bank said.
The bank also sold 178 million zlotys of its 14-percent five-year bonds after banks placed 202 million worth of bids.
The central bank offered 161 million zlotys of the shorter bonds and 178 million zlotys of the longer paper.
The minimum price of the two-year paper was 99.43, up from 99.39 on August 26 and the average price was 99.46, up from 99.43.
The minimum price of the five-year bond was 90.14, down from 90.15 on August 26 and the average price was 90.17, down from 90.19.
The settlement date is August 28, 1996 by 0900 local time.
